content: Nabilone is prescribed to manage nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy in patients who have not responded adequately to other anti-nausea medications. It belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids and works by influencing the brain areas responsible for controlling nausea and vomiting. Nabilone is available as an oral capsule and can be taken with or without food, typically 2-3 times daily during a chemotherapy cycle. Treatment should begin 1-3 hours before the first chemotherapy dose and may continue for up to 48 hours after the chemotherapy cycle ends. It is important to take nabilone at the same times each day and follow the prescription instructions carefully. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than directed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and adjust it as needed. Even if you are not experiencing nausea or vomiting, continue taking nabilone as prescribed. This medication may be habit-forming, so do not take larger doses, use it more often, or take it for a longer duration than instructed. If you feel the need to take extra medication, contact your doctor immediately. Nabilone may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking nabilone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nabilone, other cannabinoids (e.g., dronabinol or marijuana), any other medications, or any ingredients in nabilone capsules. Ask your pharmacist for a list of ingredients. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention medications such as antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, fluoxetine), antihistamines, amphetamines, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), barbiturates, benzodiazepines (e.g., diazepam), narcotics, muscle relaxants, and others. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you or your family have a history of alcohol or drug use, mental illnesses such as bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or depression, or if you have a history of high blood pressure, heart, liver, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking nabilone, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking nabilone. Nabilone may cause drowsiness, mood changes, memory issues, or altered judgment and behavior. These effects can persist for up to 72 hours after completing treatment. You should be supervised by a responsible adult during and for several days after treatment. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in dangerous activities while taking nabilone and for several days after stopping it. Do not consume alcohol while taking nabilone, as it can worsen side effects. Nabilone may also cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting when standing up too quickly. To prevent this, rise slowly from a lying position and rest your feet on the floor before standing. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking nabilone. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Nabilone may cause side effects. Mild side effects include headache, dizziness, unsteady walking, drowsiness, sleep problems, weakness, dry mouth, appetite changes, nausea, elevated mood, difficulty concentrating, anxiety, confusion, or depression. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include a fast heartbeat, hallucinations, or difficulty thinking clearly and understanding reality. If you experience these, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while taking nabilone to your doctor. Store nabilone in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. Store nabilone securely to prevent accidental or intentional use by others. Keep track of the number of capsules to ensure none are missing. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the person has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include a fast heartbeat, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, hallucinations, anxiety, changes in thinking or behavior, confusion, slowed breathing, or coma. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. This prescription is not refillable, so ensure you see your doctor for a new prescription before starting each chemotherapy cycle.
